scope: real native source signature/proof, actual isolated owner consents; nonexistent synthetic inputs
milestone: Private source authorization and exact-byte crash recovery
commands: python3 -m py_compile scripts/public_source.py scripts/public_source_guard.py scripts/public_source_release.py scripts/check_public_source_release.py scripts/check_public_authority.py
limitations: New F/C/R proofs use nonexistent synthetic note and auxiliary inputs. Native cryptography and owner signatures are real; no source reservation or public funding is fabricated.
Actual SIGKILL occurs after the durable release marker and before complete raw publication; this does not identify the exact CPU instruction at which the signature was computed.
The final descriptor-handling adjustment was rebuilt and checked by retained-byte inspection, invalid-descriptor refusal and inherited-lock retention; a second new proof graph was unnecessary.
The Python wrapper invokes live preflight under locks, but a funded public positive preflight/source-signing integration has not executed. Native signing itself does not verify live observations.
Private raw bytes and journals are retained locally and excluded from Git. Private signature preparation never grants permission to broadcast; public senders remain disabled.
Offline resume may finish the already committed decision after a deadline. A future sender must enforce fresh first-send windows and reconcile uncertain prior exposure.
Owner/original path denial and inherited lock checks ran on one macOS host, not independently administered hosts.
Local rollback/deletion and spending through another source-wallet application remain outside the guard guarantee.
